categories.main_business_segments: Eversource Energy operates four primary business segments: electric distribution, electric transmission, natural gas distribution, and water distribution. The company also has an offshore wind business, which is in the process of being divested. These segments are managed through wholly-owned regulated utility subsidiaries serving Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Eversource's core operations rely on regulated utility infrastructure for the distribution and transmission of electricity, natural gas, and water. The company utilizes advanced grid modernization, system resiliency measures, and energy efficiency technologies, and owns and operates solar power facilities. It also invests in emerging technologies such as energy storage, automation, and geothermal pilot programs.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company primarily serves residential, commercial, industrial, municipal, and fire protection customers. Its key end markets are the energy and water utility sectors in New England, with a focus on retail energy delivery and utility services for homes, businesses, and municipalities.
categories.geographic_coverage: Eversource operates mainly in the New England region, specifically in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire. Its service territories cover major metropolitan areas including Boston, Springfield, and the greater Hartford area, as well as numerous cities and towns across these states.
categories.supply_chain_position: Eversource operates downstream in the supply chain, focusing on the distribution and transmission of electricity, natural gas, and water to end users. It does not own generation assets (except for solar facilities and offshore wind investments) and procures energy and gas from competitive suppliers for delivery to customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include grid modernization, system resiliency, clean energy transition, and decarbonization. Eversource invests in infrastructure upgrades, advanced metering, energy efficiency, renewable energy integration, and pilots alternative technologies such as geothermal and energy storage. It is also focused on supporting state and federal climate goals and enhancing customer experience.
categories.revenue_model: Eversource generates revenue primarily through regulated rates for the distribution and transmission of electricity, natural gas, and water. Its revenue streams include base distribution rates, tracked cost recovery mechanisms, and regulated returns on capital investments. The company also earns revenue from solar energy sales and, until divestiture, offshore wind project interests.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Eversource is one of the largest energy delivery companies in New England and competes with other regional utilities such as National Grid and Avangrid. It holds a leading market position in its core service territories, with exclusive franchise rights for electric, gas, and water distribution in most areas it serves.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Eversource reported operating revenues of approximately $11.9 billion and serves about 4.4 million customers. The company projects long-term earnings per share growth of 5-7% from its regulated utility businesses and plans capital expenditures of over $23 billion from 2024 to 2028, indicating a significant ongoing investment and growth trajectory.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Eversource emphasizes reliable, safe, and sustainable energy and water delivery, superior customer service, and leadership in clean energy transition. Its differentiation lies in its scale, regulatory expertise, commitment to infrastructure modernization, and proactive investments in grid resiliency and decarbonization to support regional climate goals.
